standard.title: Identify Origin and Content of Sources, Explain Purpose and Context
standard.description: identify the origin, content, context and purpose of primary and secondary sources
standard.prior_knowledge: In Year 7 students identified origin, content, context and purpose of sources (AC9HH7S03). In Year 8 they continued this (AC9HH8S03). Y9 extends this by adding explanation of context (when/where produced, contemporaneous vs retrospective) and analysis of literal and symbolic features, purpose, and inferences from visual sources.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students identify the origin, content, context and purpose of primary and secondary sources, including explaining contextual features and analysing intent.

nodes.label: Identifying origin, content and context
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify the origin, content and context of primary and secondary sources, including whether a source was produced at the same time as the event or retrospectively.
nodes.minimum_width: For one source, identify: who created it (origin), what it contains (content), and when and where it was produced (context).
nodes.typical_width: Identify the context of sources — when and where produced, and whether contemporaneous with the event or retrospective; identify origin (author, organisation, context of creation) and content (what the source contains, both literal and implied); apply this across a range of source types (photographs, diaries, newspapers, government records, secondary accounts).
wider: Compare a contemporaneous source with a retrospective account of the same event — examining how time, distance, and changed context shaped what each source includes and how it frames events
Analyse sources from both coloniser and colonised perspectives on the same colonial event — practising origin/content/context analysis across very different source types and social positions
Apply origin/content/context analysis to a digital source (e.g. a digitised newspaper from Trove) and reflect on how digitisation affects the source's accessibility and the way it is read

response_modes.reason: Students frequently conflate content (what the source says) with purpose (why it was created) — explicit modelling of the distinction between these categories is necessary. The contemporaneous/retrospective distinction is new at Y9 and needs direct instruction.

success_criteria: Identifies the origin, content and context of at least one source with accuracy
Distinguishes between whether the source was produced contemporaneously with the event or retrospectively, and explains why this matters

nodes.label: Explaining purpose and analysing intent
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain the purpose of a source and analyse the intent of its author, including identifying literal and symbolic features of visual sources.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain the purpose of one source and identify at least one feature of it (literal, symbolic, or rhetorical) that reveals the author's intent.
nodes.typical_width: Identify literal and symbolic features of sources and explain their purpose and inferences; explain the events, ideas and individuals represented in visual sources; analyse the intent of the author and purpose of the source across a range of types (propaganda posters, official reports, diaries, photographs, newspaper editorials).
wider: Examine a propaganda source (e.g. a WWI recruitment poster or a colonial illustration) in depth — identifying its literal content, symbolic features, intended audience, and what it reveals about the ideological context of its production

Compare the stated purpose and the implied intent of an official document — examining the gap between what the source claims to do and what it actually reveals about the author's values or the context of its production

Analyse the intent of an author from a marginalised group (e.g. a First Nations petition, a letter from a colonial subject) alongside an official source about the same subject — examining how purpose and intent differ when access to voice is unequal

response_modes.reason: Applying purpose and intent analysis to different source types — visual, textual, official, personal — develops the skill as a transferable analytical tool rather than a template applied to one source type.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Purpose and intent analysis is the gateway skill to understanding how sources are constructed rather than simply received — practising it across many source types (propaganda, official records, personal diaries, visual sources) builds genuine historical source literacy.
success_criteria: Explains the purpose of at least one source and identifies at least one feature (literal, symbolic, or rhetorical) that reveals the author's intent
Analyses the intent of an author with reference to specific features of the source, not just general statements about bias
